lotteries.justification: New shape (certain option is a low-energy timed key-engager, never used as C before). Reward returns: C=TimedPress +659.49, A=Neutral hover +752.07 (good branch), B=Slam +293.12 (bad branch). Indifference p* = (659.49-293.12)/(752.07-293.12) = 0.798. At p=0.78 the lottery EV = 0.78*752.07 + 0.22*293.12 = 651.1, so the reward prefers certain C by ~8. A person is offered: keep a trajectory that quietly plays the keys in rhythm, or gamble on 78% pure stillness vs 22% keyboard-mashing. The reward is nearly indifferent; a musician would likely keep the engager, a minimize-mistakes view might gamble on the stillness.

lotteries.justification: New shape -- all three options are low-energy and the return range is tight, probing risk attitude at very low good-branch probability. Reward returns: C=RightHandTimedPress +670.79, A=Neutral hover +752.07 (good branch), B=TimedPress (two hands) +651.49 (bad branch). Indifference p* = (670.79-651.49)/(752.07-651.49) = 0.192. At p=0.18 the lottery EV = 0.18*752.07 + 0.82*651.49 = 669.6, so the reward prefers certain C by ~1.2 -- essentially a coin-toss-level preference. Certain single-hand engagement vs an 18%/82% gamble between doing nothing and two-hand engagement. The reward resolves a near-tie purely on expected return, where a person might have a firm preference about which style of (non-)playing they want.
